title: Why can't I sleep?
summary_es: En un programa de radio, una médica explica por qué dormimos menos que antes y qué pequeños cambios ayudan a dormir mejor.
prediction_prompt: A doctor gives advice about sleeping better. What advice do you expect to hear?

segments.speaker: mark
segments.text: Welcome back. Today we're talking about sleep with Doctor Anna Lee.

segments.speaker: mark
segments.text: Anna, do people sleep less than they used to?

segments.speaker: anna
segments.text: Yes, a little. Fifty years ago, most adults used to sleep about eight hours a night.

segments.speaker: mark
segments.text: And now?

segments.speaker: anna
segments.text: Now the average is closer to seven, and many people get less than six.

segments.speaker: mark
segments.text: Why has it changed?

segments.speaker: anna
segments.text: There are several reasons, but the biggest one is probably our phones.

segments.speaker: mark
segments.text: Because of the light from the screen?

segments.speaker: anna
segments.text: Partly, yes. Bright light tells your brain that it's still daytime.

segments.speaker: anna
segments.text: But the main problem is that phones keep our minds busy when we should be relaxing.

segments.speaker: mark
segments.text: I used to read in bed. Now I check my messages instead.

segments.speaker: anna
segments.text: You're not the only one! Reading a book is much better for you.

segments.speaker: mark
segments.text: What about coffee? I drink quite a lot of it.

segments.speaker: anna
segments.text: Coffee stays in your body for hours. I'd avoid it after two in the afternoon.

segments.speaker: mark
segments.text: Really? I often have one after dinner.

segments.speaker: anna
segments.text: Then that could be why you don't sleep well!

segments.speaker: mark
segments.text: Fair enough. What else can we do?

segments.speaker: anna
segments.text: Go to bed and get up at the same time every day, even at weekends.

segments.speaker: mark
segments.text: Even on Sundays? That's the hard part.

segments.speaker: anna
segments.text: I know, but your body loves routine. After two weeks it becomes much easier.

segments.speaker: mark
segments.text: And what if I wake up in the middle of the night?

segments.speaker: anna
segments.text: Don't look at the clock. If you can't sleep after twenty minutes, get up and do something quiet.

segments.speaker: mark
segments.text: So no phone, no late coffee and a regular routine.

segments.speaker: anna
segments.text: Exactly. Small changes can make a big difference.

segments.speaker: mark
segments.text: Doctor Lee, thank you. I'll try it tonight, starting with the coffee.

connected_speech.explanation_es: *used to* suena /ˈjuːstə/: la *d* no se pronuncia. Y *than* es débil (/ðən/).

connected_speech.phrase: used to sleep about eight hours
I used to read in bed
connected_speech.explanation_es: Otra vez /ˈjuːstə/. Es un hábito del pasado que ya no tiene.

connected_speech.phrase: get up at the same time
connected_speech.explanation_es: *get up at* se dice seguido y *at* es débil.
En *can't* la *t* casi no suena: la pista es la vocal fuerte, frente a *can* /kən/.
